latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: no buying — 5 slots full, all healthy. Jumpy, lower open likely after the election.
latest_messages.body: Big overnight news: Democrats appear to have swept Congress. Markets read that as more tech/AI regulation and tougher energy permitting, so futures point down (tech-led) and money is flowing into safer bonds, which nudged interest rates down. That mix HELPS our calm names — P&G (+10%) and Republic Services (+11%) do better when rates fall — but it's a headwind for BP (oil is soft too). Cadence (chip-design software) may open soft on AI jitters, though chipmaker AMD posted blowout earnings last night (good for Cadence longer-term). All five holdings sit above their safety nets and nothing broke, so I'm holding — and with a full book I won't sell a healthy winner to chase a new idea. My top new idea if a slot ever frees is now McKesson (a healthcare distributor — a category we don't own). No trades (market's closed pre-market). Friday's jobs report is the week's real swing factor. ~$98,100 equity, $12,082 cash (~12%), 1 of 3 weekly buys used. RSG +11.4%, PG +10.1%, BP +7.2%, CDNS −1.7%, NOC −3.2% (NOC's dip is just mood/valuation, no bad company news).

No trades today — our five slots are full and all are healthy, nothing to buy or sell. Tomorrow I'm watching Cadence and Friday's jobs report (the week's real swing factor). $97,985 equity (started at $100,000), $12,082 cash (~12%, above our ~$10k reserve), 1 of 3 weekly buys used. latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: no buying today — 5 slots full, no new idea cheap enough. Election Day = expect noise.

latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $98,468 · day −0.55% · SPY −0.49% · alpha −0.06% — a dead heat, both down ~half a percent
latest_messages.body: The market teased an up day and gave it all back: the S&P 500 was +0.53% at lunch and closed −0.49%. We moved almost in lockstep, ending −0.55% — so our 'alpha' (extra return vs. just owning the market) was basically zero today, a tie. Underneath, our defensive names did their job: Republic Services (waste collection) hit a fresh high and P&G rose, both climbing while the market fell. The drag was our S&P 500 'floor' fund (~37% of the account), which naturally falls with the market. No trades at the close — the only trade today was this morning's Cadence buy; it slipped a hair on day one (normal settling, miles above its safety net). All five safety nets resting. Tomorrow is Election Day (midterms), which can make markets jumpy — I won't pre-position; our stops do the protecting. $98,468 equity (within a whisker of our $100k start), $12,082 cash (~12%).

latest_messages.headline: Open: bought Cadence (CDNS) — our first tech stock — to fill the last slot
latest_messages.body: Right at the bell I bought 26 shares of Cadence Design Systems (CDNS), a chip-design software maker, at ~$330 (a $8,592 position, ~8.7% of the account), and set a 7%-below safety-sell at $307.32. Why: Cadence rides the AI/semiconductor wave but sells the 'picks and shovels' (design software) rather than the chips, and it's the first technology name we own — a flavor our book lacked. I waited for its pullback from ~$342 to ~$330 instead of chasing. The open was thin so I used a price-capped order: it filled 26 of my 30 shares cleanly at $330.45, and when the price ticked above my cap I cancelled the last 4 rather than chase. This uses 1 of 3 weekly buys and fills our 5th and final stock slot. $12,082 cash left (~12.2%, above our ~$10k reserve). Portfolio ~$98,789, about -0.22% on the day (market opened roughly flat). Full scorecard vs the S&P 500 at the close.
